newsitem.title: USA: District of Columbia CFO outlines upcoming audit.
newsitem.headline: District of Columbia CFO outlines upcoming audit.

text.p: District of Columbia auditors will report next week that the city is failing to collect millions of dollars in taxes from businesses and continues to have liquidity problems, the district's chief financial officer told Reuters on Friday.

Still, Anthony Williams, hired in late 1995 under federal legislation creating the city's financial control board, said that the district's fiscal problems could not have been solved in one year. And he predicted that, by next year, the city's finances will not draw significant criticism.
Williams was commenting on an audit on the city's fiscal 1996 financial statement due out February 4 from KPMG Peat Marwick, the city's independent auditor.
Williams said that the report will give the city a "qualified opinion," charging that officials did not correct two of the three problems that Peat Marwick identified in last year's audit.
The two problems are that the city has yet to collect up to $40 million owed by local businesses and that it still does not have nearly enough ready cash available for short-term expenses.

"We have a number of serious problems that we inherited," Williams said. "Everything is broken. Everybody agrees with that." But the answer is to find long-term, sustainable solutions, rather than to do a quick fixup, he said.

"It would be stupid not to take the opportunity" to do a "comprehensive" revamping of the city's financial system, Williams said. Otherwise, Williams said, he would be "frittering away" the city's chances of a real recovery in coming years.

Williams added his leadership last year did produce some "powerful results." He said he took such key steps as reducing substantially a crushing deficit in payments to key city vendors and reduced the projected deficit of $116 million to $75 million. "Where I come from that's a signficant achievement," Williams said.
